Each category encapsulates a distinct but interconnected mathematical structure. Forecast evaluation uses Murphy decomposition to separate reliability, resolution, and uncertainty into interpretable components that define forecast skill. Portfolio optimization relies on Whitrow’s Kelly solver to compute optimal allocations across correlated assets, enabling simultaneous betting strategies. MLOps artifacts define feature schemas for real-time odds ingestion, supporting automated model retraining pipelines. Research workflows utilize pre-registration templates and model cards to ensure reproducibility and transparency. These primitives form a dualistic system: one layer for probabilistic inference (GSI), another for strategic decision-making (GSE). Failure modes arise when assumptions break—e.g., non-stationary correlations invalidate Whitrow’s solver, or missing attribution data undermines adversarial validation.
